earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct ancient language of Noricum, attested in a couple of inscriptions (Eichner et al. 1994); no phonological description possible.

new_statements.quote: Die nicht nur in Noricum verbreitete Variante BELINOS ist zwar relativchronologisch jünger, da sie aus der Grundform BELENOS entstand, dennoch kann sie in vielen Fällen absolutchronologisch recht alt sein, weil sie durch den archaischen, vorgallischen Antepaenultima-Akzent bedingt wurde: BÉLENOS > BÉLINOS. – Mit der Zeit und der gallischen Paenultima-Betonung entstand aus der Grundform BÉLENOS eine modernere Variante BELÉNOS, die u. a. durch das italienische Toponym Blénio mit vortoniger Synkope fortgesetzt wird.
new_statements.translation: The variant BELINOS, widespread not only in Noricum, is relatively younger, since it arose from the base form BELENOS; nevertheless it can in many cases be quite old in absolute terms, because it was conditioned by the archaic, pre-Gaulish antepenultimate accent: BÉLENOS > BÉLINOS. – In time, with the Gaulish penultimate stress, a more modern variant BELÉNOS arose from the base form BÉLENOS, continued e.g. by the Italian toponym Blénio with pretonic syncope.

De Bernardo Stempel explains Norican theonym variants by reconstructed Continental Celtic accent stages ('vorgallischer Antepaenultima-Akzent', 'gallische Paenultima-Betonung') - a claim about Celtic/Gaulish accent chronology applied to epigraphic names, not a statement of Noric word stress; both stages are invoked for different Norican forms. | checker: OAPEN REST record for handle 20.500.12657/22373 (Hainzmann; Verlag der OeAW 2020-02; 542 pp; FWF open access) confirmed via library.oapen.org/rest/search (landing page itself is behind an Anubis bot wall); DNB SRU also lists 'Die Gottheiten in ihren sprachlichen und kultischen Erscheinungsformen / de…
new_statements.relation_note: Applies De Bernardo Stempel's Continental Celtic accent chronology (archaic antepenultimate stress, later Gaulish penultimate stress) to about eight Norican theonyms; no tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-order reconstruction: Norican theonym variants are explained by an archaic (pre-Gaulish) Celtic accent on the antepenultimate syllable (BÉLENOS > BÉLINOS, ÉRCURA without epenthesis, TOUTATIS), with the later 'Gaulish' shift to penultimate stress also invoked for other Norican forms (ADSALLUTA gemination retained after the shift; BELÍNOS > BALÍNOS). No statement of a synchronic word-stress rule for Noric as such; the author treats Norican Celtic as preserving relatively archaic (proparoxytone-stage) forms.
new_statements.exceptions: UXELLIMOS: gemination may reflect either antepenult stress of *UXÉLO-MO-S or penult stress already in UXELLOS (p. 299); NEMNICOS/Nemneci vs Nebnicca: proparoxytone vs penultimate readings both possible (p. 357).
new_statements.identity_note: Linguistic commentary on every indigenous divine name and epithet attested in the Roman province of Noricum (the onomastic corpus that, with the Ptuj and Grafenstein texts, constitutes 'Noric'); the accent remarks are De Bernardo Stempel's Continental-Celtic reconstruction applied to Norican forms, not a description of a spoken variety. | Onomastic study of Celtic (and Italic) personal and divine names from Noricum, Pannonia and N. Italy in Latin epigraphy (elvima x3 Noricum, i.o.m. Uxellimo Rimske Toplice, saxami Virunum, venim[a] Teufenbach, voltisemae); the stress hypothesis is formulated for Common/Continental Celtic, with Norican forms as evidence. | Ch. 3 'Fonološki opis' treats the 'East Celtic'/Norico-Pannonian material (incl. personal names attested only in Noricum-Pannonia: Uercombogius, Deuignata, Orceti-, Mogeti-) and concludes it must be treated within Gaulish as an undifferentiated system; the accent remark concerns these Norico-Pannonian compound names.

new_statements.quote: Interestingly, the independent testimony of elvima (three times in Noricum, see above section 5) from *φelu-isamo- points in the same direction: it must have been created after the accent system had been regularized and superlatives in -ísamo- were the norm (see below). [...] Eventually, all the superlatives containing the allomorphs -amo-, -tamo-, -samo- or -isamo- became proparoxytone, either obeying new constraints on the position of stress or because the place of the stress in this particular formation was assigned to any vowel preceding the common recognizable sequence -(C)amo-.

Prosper's accent claims concern the Common/Continental Celtic superlative formation (-isamo- becoming proparoxytone), reconstructed from syncope across Pannonia, Noricum and N. Italy; Norican elvima is one datum. Not a statement about word stress in Noric as a language, and second-order reconstruction at that. | checker: Crossref and DOAJ records confirm Prósper 2018, Voprosy onomastiki 15(2): 108-138, doi:10.15826/vopr_onom.2018.15.2.017, open PDF at onomastics.ru. In the saved text the first quoted sentence ('the independent testimony of elvima (three times in Noricum..).. superlatives in -ísamo- were the norm') is verbatim on p. 129 and the second…
new_statements.relation_note: Stress-conditioned syncope model for Celtic comparative/superlative names including Norican examples; no tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-order reconstruction: Common Celtic superlatives in -isamo- were originally pre-proparoxytone (stress on the 4th-last syllable), later all superlatives became proparoxytone with stress attracted to -í(samo)-, causing syncope of the following /a/; Norican elvima (< *φelu-ísamo-) is said to postdate this regularisation. A claim about accent in one morphological class of Continental Celtic names, not a word-stress rule for Noric.
new_statements.exceptions: clussimi/Osismi fail to syncopate medial i (early -st- context); rigisamo unsyncopated 'or analogical'; voltisemae in Noricum classed as non-Celtic.

new_statements.quote: Noriško-panonska antroponimija keltskega izvora, kot je dobro znano, sicer izkazuje številna osebna lastna imena, ki se zunaj tega areala ne pojavljajo, prim. Uer-com-bogius, Deui-gnata, Orceti- (KPP: 252), Mogeti- (Corpus, ss. 164–165) ipd., a se ob tem vsaj v primeru trizložnih zaporedij *Moget-o-, *Orcet-o- zdi, da je v izstopajočih različicah morda treba prepoznati le odraz drugotne šibitve nenaglašenega veznega samoglasnika. Na to možnost opozarjata zlasti različici Mogitu-marus (CIL XII/731) in Mogit-marus (CIL III/3325, prim. KPP: 111), ki nedvomno kažeta na šibitev -o- v prednaglasnem zlogu in celo njegovo popolno onemitev v sinkopirani različici Mogit- (gl. De Bernardo Stempel 2013a: 64, Sims-Williams 2015: 325).
new_statements.translation: Norico-Pannonian anthroponymy of Celtic origin, as is well known, shows numerous personal names that do not occur outside this area, cf. Uer-com-bogius, Deui-gnata, Orceti-, Mogeti- etc., but at least in the case of the trisyllabic sequences *Moget-o-, *Orcet-o- it seems that the deviant variants may reflect merely a secondary weakening of the unstressed linking vowel. This possibility is pointed to especially by the variants Mogitu-marus (CIL XII/731) and Mogit-marus (CIL III/3325), which undoubtedly show weakening of -o- in the pretonic syllable and even its complete loss in the syncopated variant Mogit- (see De Bernardo Stempel 2013a: 64, Sims-Williams 2015: 325).
new_statements.citation: Repanšek, Luka. 2016. Keltska dediščina v toponimiji jugovzhodnega alpskega prostora. (Linguistica et philologica 33.) Ljubljana: Založba ZRC, ZRC SAZU. doi:10.3986/9789610504139. [re-listing of A#3: the open-but-'silent' work does contain accent-bearing remarks on Norican names]

new_statements.relation_note: One sentence attributing vowel weakening/syncope in Norico-Pannonian compound names to pretonic position; one footnote rejecting an accent-based (post-tonic gemination) etymology of ADSALLUTA; no tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Passing second-order inference only: in Norico-Pannonian Gaulish compound names of the type Mogitu-marus/Mogit-marus the compositional vowel stood in a pretonic (unstressed) syllable and was weakened or syncopated, i.e. the stress lay after it (on the second member); the author otherwise treats the East Celtic/Noric material as plain Gaulish and explicitly rejects one of De Bernardo Stempel's accent-based explanations of a Norican theonym (Adsalluta). No word-stress rule for Noric is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: Magi-marus beside Magio-marus (p. 51) is said NOT to be conditioned by syncope or other secondary sound change.
